title: Lebanese council at Baabda proclaims independence
why: A Lebanese assembly met at Baabda and declared independence months before France proclaimed Greater Lebanon.

title: Arrêté 299 attaches Bekaa and Hasbaya cazas to Lebanon
why: Decree linking the cazas of Hasbaya, Rachaya, Maallaka and Baalbek to Lebanon, a step toward the 1920 borders.

title: Arrêté 318 delimits the borders of Greater Lebanon
why: Gouraud's decree fixed the territorial extent of Greater Lebanon, the basis of today's borders.

title: Gouraud leaves; Robert de Caix acts as High Commissioner
why: Henri Gouraud's term ended; de Caix served as acting High Commissioner until April 1923.

title: Maxime Weygand becomes High Commissioner
why: Weygand held the post until 29 Nov 1924, during the early mandate consolidation.

title: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon formally enters into force
why: The League of Nations mandate took legal effect after the 1922 confirmation and Franco-British boundary settlement.

title: First official religious census of Greater Lebanon conducted
why: The 1922 count produced the early sectarian baseline later contrasted with the 1932 census.

title: Maurice Sarrail becomes High Commissioner
why: Sarrail served until December 1925; his tenure coincided with the outbreak of the Great Syrian Revolt.

title: Henry de Jouvenel becomes High Commissioner
why: Held the post from 23 Dec 1925 to 23 June 1926, spanning the promulgation of the 1926 constitution.

title: Great Syrian Revolt spills into Rashaya area
why: The Druze-led revolt against French rule reached the Lebanese border area, including a battle at Rashaya.

title: Auguste Ponsot becomes High Commissioner
why: Ponsot held office until 16 July 1933.

title: Damien de Martel becomes High Commissioner
why: De Martel served until January 1939, a span covering the 1936 Franco-Lebanese treaty.

title: Gabriel Puaux becomes High Commissioner
why: Puaux held the post through the constitution suspension of 1939 until November 1940. (corrected from 1939-01; he took office 22 Oct 1938)

title: Henri Dentz becomes Vichy High Commissioner
why: Dentz led Vichy administration in Lebanon until the Allied conquest in June 1941.

title: Georges Catroux becomes Free French delegate-general
why: Catroux ran Free French authority until 7 June 1943 and proclaimed independence in Nov 1941.

title: Jean Helleu becomes Free French delegate-general
why: Helleu served until 23 Nov 1943, the day after the Lebanese leaders were released.

title: Yves Chataigneau replaces Helleu as French delegate-general
why: Appointed the day after the Lebanese leaders' release to manage the transfer of powers.

title: Paul Beynet becomes French delegate-general
why: Beynet held office until 1 Sep 1946, covering the transfer of services and the troop evacuation.

title: Antoun Saadeh founds the Syrian Social Nationalist Party
why: Founded in secret and public from 1932; his biography page dates the secret founding to November 1932.

title: SSNP starts publishing the monthly Al-Majalla
why: The journal developed the party's ideology after it went public.

title: French authorities jail Saadeh for six months
why: He was imprisoned for creating a clandestine party.

title: SSNP launches its first armed revolt against the government
why: The attempted uprising preceded the arrest and 8 July execution of Antoun Saadeh.

title: Pierre Gemayel founds the Kataeb Party
why: A Maronite-led youth movement modelled on European party youth groups, it became a major Lebanese party.

title: Kataeb drafts first Lebanese party labour charter
why: Proposed minimum wage, working-hour limits and paid leave.

title: Kataeb creates first women's section in a Lebanese party
why: The section campaigned against gender discrimination.

title: Syrian-Lebanese Communist Party founded
why: Founded by Yusuf Yazbek, Fuad al-Shamali and Artin Madoyan; in Lebanon it first used the name Lebanese People's Party.

title: Mandate ban on Communist Party relaxed again
why: After a first relaxation under the Popular Front, authorities again eased restrictions on the party.

title: Communists contest first independent-era election and win no seat
why: The party failed to win any seat; its Lebanese and Syrian branches were formally split by late 1943.

title: Communist Party outlawed in Lebanon
why: The party was outlawed in 1948, after taking part in the 1943 legislative elections.

title: Najjadeh Party begins as a Sunni scout organisation
why: Founded in 1933-34 by Muhi al-Din al-Nasuli as a counterweight to the Kataeb.

title: Adnan al-Hakim reorganises Najjadeh into a political party
why: Under his lead it grew quickly with a pan-Arab motto.

title: Bechara el-Khoury founds the Constitutional Bloc
why: The bloc pursued independence from French rule and later anchored the National Pact camp.

title: Émile Eddé constitutes the National Bloc as a party
why: Created as an election bloc in 1943, it became a formal party in 1946.

title: Battle of the Litani River in the Syria-Lebanon campaign
why: Allied forces fought Vichy French units in south Lebanon.

title: Battles of Jezzine and Sidon
why: Allied forces advanced on the coast and into the mountains of south Lebanon.

title: Battle of Damour begins
why: Fighting on the coast south of Beirut lasted until 9 July.

title: Ceasefire ends fighting in the Syria-Lebanon campaign
why: A ceasefire took effect one minute past midnight after Dentz sought an armistice on 10 July.

title: Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre signed
why: Ended Vichy control of Lebanon and Syria.

title: First Lebanese flag raised in Bechamoun
why: Raised on the day French authorities arrested the president and ministers.

title: Iraq Petroleum Company oil first reaches Tripoli terminal
why: The Kirkuk pipeline's Tripoli branch delivered crude to Lebanon's coast.

title: First tanker loads IPC crude at Tripoli
why: The French tanker Henry Desprez left Tripoli with the first shipment.

title: Tripoli holds official opening ceremony for the IPC pipeline
why: One of five January 1935 opening ceremonies along the line.

title: High Commissioner announces plan for a tobacco monopoly
why: De Martel said France would replace the banderole system with a state monopoly.

title: Tobacco workers petition against the planned monopoly
why: A petition represented five thousand tobacco workers and their families.

title: Week of protests against the tobacco monopoly
why: Strikes and demonstrations in Beirut, Tripoli, Homs and Damascus, with women tobacco workers the majority.

title: Decision approves the Franco-Lebanese-Syrian tobacco Régie company
why: Authorised a company with capital of 1,250,000 Syrian-Lebanese pounds holding the tobacco monopoly.

title: Tobacco Régie established and Cahier des Charges finalised
why: The monopoly displaced 1,500 to 3,000 cigarette factory workers.

title: Beirut tramway and electricity boycott
why: A boycott targeted the French-Belgian concession company over prices and service.

title: Beirut tramway and electricity boycott spreads to other cities
why: Described as the first time Beirut's classes and confessional communities acted together; it spread to Damascus.

title: Beirut tram and electricity company becomes mainly French-owned
why: The Ottoman-era concession passed from Belgian to French control.

title: Properties transferred to Société des Tramways et de l'Éclairage de Beyrouth
why: The company was later renamed Électricité de Beyrouth.

title: Protests target the Beirut electricity company during political mobilisation
why: Electricity and tram protests recurred in 1936, 1943 and 1946.

title: British engineers complete standard-gauge Haifa-Beirut railway
why: Built for the Allied war effort; it never served civilian traffic.

title: Wartime rail extension to Tripoli completed
why: Completed the Haifa-Beirut-Tripoli line.

title: Lebanon buys the Naqoura-Tripoli railway line
why: Lebanon later reorganised its network as the state railway.

title: French authorities give Banque de Syrie the note-issue privilege
why: It acted as central bank for the mandate territories until the Banque du Liban in 1963.

title: Middle East Airlines starts operations
why: First route linked Beirut and Nicosia, then Iraq, Egypt and Syria, using three Dragon Rapides.

title: Pan American acquires a stake and management contract in MEA
why: Foreign capital entered the new Lebanese airline.

title: Troupes Spéciales du Levant reach about 10,000 troops
why: Locally recruited units numbered 306 officers, only 88 of them French.

title: Lebanese Armed Forces formally take over from French authority
why: Command passed at 00:00; the date is Army Day.

title: Lebanese army battalion takes Qadas and Malkieh
why: Its first major combat; the army withdrew by 8 July 1948.

title: Beirut Traders Association founded
why: An early business body of the mandate era.

title: Al Joumhouria newspaper launches in Beirut
why: Added to the capital's growing Arabic press.

title: L'Orient founded by Gabriel Khabbaz and Georges Naccache
why: The French-language daily later merged with Le Jour into L'Orient-Le Jour.

title: National Conservatory of Music established in Beirut
why: An early public institution for music teaching.

title: American Junior College for Women opens in Ras Beirut
why: The institution was the forerunner of the Lebanese American University.

title: Parliament building erected in Beirut
why: The building that later became the seat of the Lebanese parliament. (corrected from 1933; building completed 1934, designed by Mardiros Altounian)

title: Gebran Tueni founds An-Nahar
why: Started as a four-page hand-set paper with five staff and 500 copies.

title: Michel Chiha founds Le Jour
why: The French-language daily merged with L'Orient on 15 June 1971.

title: Beirut population about 162,000
why: Population figure for the capital in 1934.

title: National Museum of Beirut opens
why: Opened to the public during the war years.

title: Al-Hayat newspaper begins publication in Beirut
why: Launched in the first year after the French withdrawal.

title: Women first enrol at the American University of Beirut
why: Women entered medicine, pharmacy and dentistry.

title: Syrian Protestant College renamed American University of Beirut
why: The 1866 college took its present name.

title: First Lebanese film, The Adventures of Elias Mabruk, premieres
why: A silent film directed by Jordano Pidutti about an emigrant's return from America.

title: In the Ruins of Baalbeck, first Lebanese-dialect sound film
why: Produced by Luminar Films; described as the first Arab film made entirely in an Arab country.

title: Armenian refugees arrive in Lebanon in large numbers
why: The influx ran from 1918 to 1920, settling in Karantina and later Bourj Hammoud.

title: Hatay assembly votes to join Turkey
why: The Alexandretta outcome pushed Armenian refugees toward Lebanon.

title: Armenian refugees from Musa Dagh resettled at Anjar
why: Several thousand refugees founded the Bekaa town in 1939.

title: Lebanon declares war on Germany and Japan
why: Lebanon joined Egypt, Syria and Saudi Arabia in declaring war in February 1945.

title: Federation of Trade Unions of Workers and Employees founded
why: It campaigned for the first Labour Code, issued in September 1946.

title: General Syndicate of Tobacco Workers formed
why: An early labour union formed in the mandate era.

title: Women's Union in Syria and Lebanon active from this period
why: Women's organising grew in the early 1920s.

title: Wadi al-Hujeir conference rejects French guardianship
why: Jabal Amel notables led by Abd al-Husayn Sharaf al-Din called for resistance and Muslim-Christian unity.

title: Administrative Committee (1920) and Representative Council (1922) set up for Greater Lebanon
why: First legislative bodies under the mandate; Daoud Amoun led the committee, Habib Pacha Saad then spoke for the Council. (title corrected: Administrative Committee first sat 4 Oct 1920 under Amoun; Representative Council set up 1922, Habib Pacha Saad speaker from 25 May 1922, per en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habib_Pacha_Saad)

title: High Commissioner Ponsot suspends the constitution
why: Suspended to head off a Muslim president (Muhammad al-Jisr) and a budget crisis; Debbas's term was extended by a year.

title: Habib Pacha Saad appointed president for one year
why: De Martel appointed him after Debbas resigned on 2 January 1934.

title: Eddé restores part of the 1926 constitution and Chamber elections held
why: The new president partly revived the suspended constitution.

title: Chamber elects the Lebanese delegation for the treaty with France
why: Negotiations led by President Eddé and Chamber president Khalid Shihab followed.

title: Decision 89/LR authorises commemorative stamps of the 1936 treaty signing
why: The five-value set showed the Petit Sérail signing ceremony.

title: Alfred Naccache named president under Free French authority
why: Appointed the day Catroux proclaimed independence.

title: Lebanese constitution re-established
why: Restored after the 1939 suspension.

title: Franco-British agreement on withdrawal of troops from the Levant
why: Set the path to the last evacuation in 1946.

title: Decree 3339 enacts the Land Property Code
why: Redefined Ottoman land categories into a private-property regime.

title: Lebanese Code of Commerce dated 12 December 1942
why: Core commercial statute still referred to today.

title: British set up the Middle East Supply Centre
why: A clearing-house for civilian supply and shipping across the Middle East during the war.

title: Bread riots and strikes in Beirut
why: Mid-July disturbances over wheat shortages; authorities found grain for Beirut for a few days.

title: Wartime food cost up 450 percent since January 1939
why: General cost of living rose about 300 percent; 1942 was the worst year of wartime hardship.

title: Anbara Salam speaks unveiled in Beirut
why: Reported as the first Muslim woman in the Levant to do so in public; sources differ on 1927 or 1928 and the venue.

title: Official census of Greater Lebanon counts 558,900 residents
why: Christians 285,700, Muslims 225,000, Druze 39,900; the first official count under the mandate.

title: Official 1932 census: 793,400 residents, Christians 396,900
why: Muslims 333,100 and Druze 53,300; the figures behind the 6:5 confessional ratio.
dup_of: Last official census: Christians about half

title: Mandate "Common Budget" created for all states
why: Run by the High Commissioner, funded 80-90 percent by customs, it paid up to 70 percent of French military costs.

title: Syrian-Lebanese pound valued at 20 French francs
why: Local currency 1928-31, converted to francs at 20 to one in budget accounts.

title: Primary school enrolment in Lebanon reaches 142,549
why: Nearly doubled from 76,649 in 1927; Lebanon outpaced the State of Syria.

title: French authorities grant a radio-electric communication concession
why: Radio-Orient was set up in 1922 to operate it.

title: Lebanon joins the International Telecommunication Union
why: Early membership in the telecom body under the mandate.

title: First submarine telegraph cable links Beirut to Nabeul, Tunisia
why: The first undersea cable connection of Lebanon.

title: Radio-Orient begins broadcasting in Beirut
why: Run by a private company; described as the second radio station in the Arab world after Cairo.

title: Radio-Orient becomes state-run Lebanese Radio
why: Renamed under government administration after independence.

title: Bir Hassan Airfield opens as Beirut's first commercial airport
why: Opened by the mandate authorities; it served until 1950 and was expanded by the Allies in WWII.

title: Allies expand Bir Hassan into a class A airfield
why: RAF squadrons operated from it between 1941 and 1944.

title: Franco-British-Lebanese-Syrian protocol fixes the pound's parity
why: Set at 1 sterling = 8.83 Lebanese pounds = 176.60 francs; changes needed consultation.

title: Burj el-Barajneh camp set up for Palestinian refugees
why: Established by the Red Cross for refugees from Galilee; initial population about 3,500.

title: Ain al-Hilweh camp set up near Sidon
why: Established by the Red Cross to shelter refugees mostly from northern Palestine.

title: Construction of Khalde (Beirut) airport begins
why: Planned from 1945; used commercially in 1950 and inaugurated on 23 April 1954.

title: France replaces Britain as the Levant's top supplier
why: It held that position until French direct control ended in the Second World War.

title: Exports cover only 25 percent of imports for 1920-33
why: A structural trade deficit that doubled in the first mandate decade.

title: Depression halves the value of Levant trade
why: Import volumes fell only 4 percent but values fell about 50 percent on lower world prices.

title: Trade deficit returns to pre-depression levels
why: The worst depression effects were over; import coverage had ranged from 30 to 65 percent in 1930-37.

title: George Arida builds a cotton spinning mill in Tripoli
why: Funded by emigrant capital earned in Mexico; it supplied about 12 percent of Syro-Lebanese textile imports in the 1930s-40s.

title: Tourist arrivals under 30,000 a year
why: They rose to about 216,000 in 1952, a baseline for the later tourism boom.

title: Government legalises the black exchange market
why: Lebanese capital was allowed to move freely abroad, part of the liberal exchange policy.

title: 1949 Monetary Law and official gold-buying policy
why: Aimed at a stable independent currency and making Beirut a financial centre.

title: Chamber ratifies the Franco-Lebanese Monetary Accord
why: Gave access to blocked franc balances but kept costly financial ties with France.

title: Allied spending and printing money fuel wartime inflation
why: Banknotes in circulation in Syria and Lebanon rose from 47.85 million (Dec 1939) to 239 million (Oct 1943); cost of living rose about 4 times officially, a little over 5 times by estimate (corrected from 'six-fold' and 'LL55 million to LL400 million', which no readable source supports).

title: Conseil d'Etat (State Council) established
why: The administrative judiciary was created under the French mandate.

title: Mandate-era press law replaces the Ottoman 1909 law
why: A stricter law; L'Orient alone was suspended 22 times by mandate and later authorities.

title: Émile Eddé resigns the presidency
why: He resigned as Vichy authority took hold; the Free French appointed Naccache in November.

title: Armenian Catholicosate of Cilicia leases the Antelias orphanage as its seat
why: The seat moved from Sis (held since 1293) to Lebanon.

title: American relief committee opens Armenian orphanage at Antelias
why: Ran until 1928 for genocide survivors, then became the Catholicosate's seat.
actors: American Committee for Relief in the Near East

title: Armenian refugees live in Karantina and Mar Mikhael tent camps
why: Tent settlements held refugees in the 1920s before the move to the Bourj Hammoud marsh.

title: Antoun Saadeh returns to Lebanon from South America
why: He had lived abroad from 1938 and led the SSNP until his 1949 arrest.

title: Antoun Saadeh leaves for South America
why: He lived mostly in Argentina until March 1947 after repeated French arrests.

title: Lebanon votes against the UN Partition Plan for Palestine
why: Lebanon rejected the plan as it was adopted by the General Assembly.

title: Lebanese Red Cross founded
why: Recognised by the state in 1946 and joined the Red Cross federation in 1947.

title: Lebanon joins UNESCO
why: Early membership in a UN specialised agency after independence.

title: Lebanon joins the International Labour Organization
why: Membership followed the 1946 Labour Code.

title: US Johnson-Reed Act sharply cuts Lebanese immigration to the US
why: Arrivals fell to a few hundred a year, ending the first mass emigration wave.

title: First hydroelectric unit in Lebanon installed at Bechare (Kadisha)
why: The Kadisha company's first plant started electrifying North Lebanon.

title: Works start on the Richmaya-Safa hydro plant near Aley
why: The 4.5 km water gallery was dug by hand; the plant later fed the Beirut tramway.

title: Two Richmaya hydro units enter commercial service
why: Each produced 3,160 kW; the plant fed Beirut's tramway and the presidential palace.

title: Al Bared hydro concession plants in operation
why: The Nahr al-Bared plants add to North Lebanon's early hydropower.

title: IPC refinery at Tripoli starts
why: Built to process Kirkuk crude arriving by pipeline, 21,000 barrels a day.

title: Syria and Lebanon bring troop-withdrawal complaint to the UN Security Council
why: They contested the 13 December 1945 Franco-British agreement as conditioning withdrawal; debate ran 14-16 February.

title: USSR casts the first Security Council veto over Levant troops
why: The veto concerned withdrawing foreign troops from Syria and Lebanon.
